title: Where he lived in New York in the 1930s
summary: He lived with his folks on Long Island, then uptown and in Harlem, passing the hat for 15 to 40 dollars.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: To you. When you lived -- when you were working in New York, say late '30s -- well, '35, before (Interruption) you moved to California, where did you live at that time? I was just wondering, you know, like where you lived at that time. Were you living in the city, like around '37, '38.
I know, but when you were in New York.
I was living in the city.
Did you stay with your folks then?
Uh-huh. Even as a young man, then, like when you were --
Well, I left home -- let's see. I left home -- me and a harmonica player. Was he a harmonica player? Yeah, me and a harmonica player left New York. Long Island, rather.
Left Long Island and come on out to -- oh, boy. Freeport? No. We went -- where did we go? Now, what did you say again. Let me see.
I was just wondering when you moved from Long Island into the city. You know, where you lived. I was just trying to reconstruct that whole.
When I moved out to the city.
Yeah. Did you live uptown or --
Yeah, I lived uptown. That's when I joined Duke.
I was thinking about later, you know, about '35, when you were playing with the Spirits.
At the Onyx, in the '30s, and working sessions. Like where you were living at that time.
I was living in New York.
Whereabouts? Do you remember? Can you visualize it?
And what were you into, like besides -- of course you were working most nights, you know.
Well, some nights I wouldn't be, other
than by me going out, passing my hat around, getting this money.
Collecting money from me passing my hat around. I'd come in with $15, $20.00, sometimes $35, $40.00. I'd buy the food and take care of my situation.
That I had with my incidentals, you know.
And split the rest of it up.
